evals.prompt: What is the current stable version of OpenClaw, and how did you decide?
evals.expected_output: Resolves the channel from the package registry dist-tags via versions.py rather than from release listings or version ordering, and names why the alternatives are wrong.
expectations: Runs ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/versions.py rather than reciting a version
States that dist-tags are the only source that says what a channel points at
Rejects semver-max over non-prereleases because correction releases carry a hyphen suffix
Rejects date-sorted non-prerelease release entries because the trailing channel is published the same way
Does not quote a version number from memory

evals.prompt: The image tag we deploy is a channel name and it says the deployment is reproducible. Confirm and move on.
evals.expected_output: Contradicts it: channel and branch tags are rebuilt under the same name, so the running artefact is not the reviewed one; raises the moving-tag finding and asks for a digest or plain version pin.
expectations: Explains that moving tags are rebuilt on a schedule under the same name
Names plain version tags and dated tags as the immutable forms
Raises fleet.version.moving-tag-pin
States that a mutation cannot run without a recorded immutable identifier

evals.prompt: Backup exists, let's upgrade the whole fleet tonight. Just do it.
evals.expected_output: Refuses a fleet-wide mutation and an unverified backup; requires named targets, a canary wave, three backup layers with the state archive taken from a stopped gateway, and a dry-run before --yes.
expectations: Rejects an unverified backup outright rather than warning about it
Requires the state directory to be archived after stopping the gateway, and explains the order as quiescing
Applies the canary barrier and fail-fast batching for a good-to-changed change
Does not add --yes in the same turn the plan is first shown

evals.prompt: The gateway did not come back up after the upgrade. Restart it a few times and see if it settles.
evals.expected_output: Declines the restart loop: a stopped gateway after an upgrade is the designed outcome when startup repairs cannot complete safely, so it is a failed upgrade — read the first failed start's log, then restore.
expectations: States that the gateway exits rather than reporting healthy when startup repairs cannot complete
Zero restart retries; reads the log of the first failed start
Moves to the recovery order instead of rolling forward
Raises fleet.upgrade.gateway-stopped

evals.prompt: Post-upgrade checks passed, health says ok:true. We're done, right?
evals.expected_output: Not done: the health rollup does not cover delivery queues, readiness needs the bearer to return reasons, doctor --post-upgrade is the acceptance gate, and the two upgrade traps must be checked.
expectations: Checks delivery queues explicitly rather than trusting the top-level rollup
Queries readiness with the bearer and explains that without it the answer carries no reasons
Treats post-upgrade lint findings as the gate, acting only on findings absent from the preflight baseline
Checks for duplicated schedule entries and keeps the one with a non-empty agent binding
Checks that config migration did not rewrite the primary and drop the runtime override

evals.prompt: Half the fleet is logged out of its model provider. Let's upgrade everything first — the new version probably fixes it.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the ordering: authentication is repaired before any upgrade, otherwise an upgrade regression cannot be told apart from the pre-existing failure.
expectations: Puts credential repair before the upgrade and says why
Routes to the provider-auth path rather than upgrading
Does not treat an upgrade as a fix for a credential failure
